name: Windhawk
description: A debugger-attach toolkit for writing your own Windows shell and system modifications in C++, each with its own source, compiler log and one-click revert.

name: Winaero Tweaker
description: A single panel of Windows settings that Microsoft scattered across the Group Policy editor, the registry and the Settings app, each with the change shown before it is made.

name: Ultimate Windows Tweaker
description: A large catalogue of context-menu, privacy and performance toggles, presented as a list you tick rather than a registry you edit.

name: ExplorerPatcher
description: Restores the Windows 10 taskbar, Start menu and File Explorer behaviour on Windows 11. It hooks the shell, so each Windows update can break it until a matching build ships.

name: PowerToys
description: Microsoft's own suite: FancyZones window layouts, PowerToys Run launcher, Awake keep-awake, Text Extractor, FancyZones, Keyboard Manager and a colour picker.

name: StartAllBack
description: Puts a classic Start menu, taskbar and Explorer ribbon back on Windows 11 while leaving the modern shell installed underneath.

name: Start11
description: Replaces the Windows 11 Start menu and taskbar with a configurable one: vertical or horizontal layout, submenus, and per-monitor taskbars.

name: Fences 6
description: Draws named, movable, roll-up containers on the desktop so icon groups can be swept aside. Paid, and the oldest tool of its kind still shipped.

name: Lively Wallpaper
description: Free, open-source animated wallpapers — video, HTML, GIF or a running app — with automatic pause when a game or full-screen app takes the screen.

name: Wallpaper Engine
description: Paid Steam title with the largest animated wallpaper library anywhere. Bought through Steam, so there is no package ID and no way to install it from here.

name: Dynamic Theme
description: Windows wallpaper and accent colour that follow the daily Bing image or the system dark and light theme, running from the tray.

name: Rainmeter
description: The long-running desktop widget engine: skins written in a small INI-like language, drawn by third parties for clocks, system meters and layouts.

name: BeWidgets
description: Home-screen style widgets for the Windows desktop — clock, weather, notes, images — free and available through the Microsoft Store.

name: TranslucentTB
description: Makes the taskbar clear, blurred, transparent or accent-coloured, and can change it per state — Start open, a window maximised, the desktop showing.

name: 7+ Taskbar Tweaker
description: Control click, grouping and scrolling behaviour of the taskbar buttons in one window. Windows 11 support depends on the build — check the project page before installing.

name: RoundedTB
description: Rounds the corners of the taskbar and shrinks it to the width of the icons. A small utility whose development has slowed — check the repository before you rely on it.

name: TaskbarX
description: Centres the taskbar icons and can give the taskbar a transparent or animated background. It watches and moves the tray, so it fights with other taskbar tweakers.

name: EarTrumpet
description: Per-application volume control in the tray: fly out every session, drag the sliders, mute one app without touching the rest.

name: komorebi
description: A tiling window manager for Windows that auto-arranges windows into workspaces and columns. Driven by its CLI and a config file rather than a settings screen.

name: GlazeWM
description: A tiling window manager for Windows modelled on i3: tree-based workspaces, keyboard-driven focus and movement, configured from one YAML file.
